comment: Shared allowlist/suppression config for the public-release audits. Deep-merges over the defaults embedded in scripts/audit_common.py. Review this file whenever the audit surfaces new findings; never silence findings by deleting the config. Allowlisted values are fabricated test fixtures (fake addresses/phone/coordinates in tests and Massachusetts ingest fixtures), the GitHub noreply committer address used for synthetic PR merge-ref commits, and '2018 Constitutional Court' (a court name, not a street address; false positive of the street-address pattern).

allowlist.tax_ids_comment: Reviewed dispositions for PII-005, which flags any long numeric run, EIN-shaped or parcel-shaped value for human review. IMPORTANT: these entries are matched as SUBSTRINGS of the detected value, not as whole values, so a short entry silences every longer match containing it. The two 9-digit entries ('301872244', '301371778') therefore also silence any 10-12 digit number containing them, because LONG_NUMERIC_RE matches 9-12 digits; prefer full-length entries. The 12-digit entries are manufacturer product identifiers on device records (UPC/EAN barcodes and article numbers), reviewed 2026-08-08 and confirmed to be published product codes. '12-3456789' is the sequential-digit documentation placeholder used as the worked example beside EIN_RE in scripts/ingest/validation.py and as the synthetic fixture in tests/test_validation.py and tests/test_massachusetts.py that proves the EIN detector fires; it is not an issued Employer Identification Number, and because EIN_RE is a fixed 10-character format a 10-character entry can only match itself. Reviewed 2026-08-13. Add an entry only after confirming the number is a published product identifier or a documentation placeholder. '628078800836' is the Arizer Solo II UPC on recalls/TRCL-0015 (Health Canada notice RA-77974), reviewed 2026-09-06 alongside the Solo III UPC already listed.
allowlist.addresses_comment: Reviewed false positives. 'Constitutional Court' matches the street-suffix pattern in legal citations such as 'the 2018 Constitutional Court ruling'; it is a court, not a street. The remaining entries are synthetic Massachusetts test-fixture addresses. Reviewed 2026-08-09. Add an entry only after confirming the match is not a real premises address.
allowlist.emails_comment: noreply@github.com and @users.noreply.github.com are GitHub-generated, non-personal addresses. beau@boorman.tech is the maintainer's own git committer identity, present in the author/committer field of every commit in this repository and already public in the GitHub commit log; it is not leaked third-party PII. Reviewed 2026-08-09.
allowlist.phones_comment: 555-01xx is the NANP block reserved for fictional use; such numbers cannot be assigned to a real subscriber and appear here only in test fixtures. 617-555-0199 is the specific fixture instance. Reviewed 2026-08-09.

suppressions_comment: Every entry is an exact CODE:path pair or a bare code; audit_common.is_suppressed does no prefix or glob matching, deliberately, so silencing N files costs N reviewable lines. Two classes, both self-detection. (1) Detector definitions: audit_sensitive_content.py and audit_common.py contain the PII regexes themselves, and test_sensitive_content_classification.py contains the synthetic PII-shaped fixtures that prove those regexes fire, including the negative controls that keep the business-contact rule from under-flagging. (2) PII-007 exclusion declarations: this file defines prohibited_fields (already suppressed before 2026-08-13), and the five entries added on 2026-08-13 cover scripts/ingest/validation.py which defines EXCLUDED_FIELD_NAMES, data/massachusetts-ccc/privacy-spec.md and source-catalog.json which are generated from EXCLUDED_FIELD_NAMES, one dated sync report recording which fields the privacy gate BLOCKED, and reports/jurisdiction-pipeline-audit.md which describes the California schema fields the pipeline drops. Each names a field in order to exclude it; none carries a value, verified by re-scanning all six paths with every allowlist and suppression disabled. CAUTION when adding more: prohibited_fields (14 names) and EXCLUDED_FIELD_NAMES (32 names) overlap on only business_email and business_phone, so PII-007 is a much narrower tripwire than it looks, and there is no name detector anywhere in the audit -- nothing else would catch an owner name. Reviewed 2026-08-13.
suppressions_history_comment: PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-08-12; the exposure is NOT over. This key formerly recorded three LARGE-004 suppressions covering ~79 MiB of California DCC licensee data reachable in git history. docs/history-cleanup-plan.md was executed and main was force-pushed on 2026-08-12T18:04:56Z, so the payloads are gone from origin/main and those suppression entries were removed. They are NOT gone from GitHub: pull-request refs were never rewritten, so the pre-rewrite history stays reachable and the registry is still fetchable from this public repository by an unauthenticated client (verified 2026-08-13). Reproduction steps and the affected object id are held with the maintainers, deliberately not in this tracked file; private vulnerability reporting is disabled on this repository, so there is no private channel to file them in yet. Do NOT re-add a suppression for this; it needs a GitHub Support request to drop the stale pull refs and expire the objects. Separately, a clone made before the rewrite reports LARGE-003/LARGE-004 from its own stale refs because those checks scan `git rev-list --all`; that part is fixed locally by deleting stale branches and running `git gc --prune=now`.
